pack.text: {"authority":{"authority_id":"khalm-reference-packs","authority_name":"KHALM reference packs"},"description":"The NIST AI Risk Management Framework 1.0 (NIST AI 100-1), in the part a v0.1 Verifiable Model Record can answer: subcategories of the MAP and MEASURE functions that ask for documented, checkable evidence about an AI system and the technology it was built from. The severity of each rule is this pack's weighting, not a claim that the voluntary Framework mandates anything.","disclaimer":"A reference implementation of the VMR policy-pack format, not legal advice and not an official instrument. The subcategory references are this pack author's reading of the cited text; the National Institute of Standards and Technology has neither authored nor endorsed this pack. The AI RMF is voluntary and covers far more than any document can check.","jurisdiction":"us-nist","pack_id":"khalm-reading-nist-ai-rmf-1.0","pack_version":"1.0.0","rules":[{"description":"The system's security and resilience can be examined for a pinned artifact in a pinned environment. Checks: what was learned is pinned by hash and size; the training software and the software hash of the environment the learning ran in are declared and not empty, and the software hash parses as a hash; and a deployment or policy-change record keeps the model of its verified immediate predecessor, the same model_hash, so one evaluated without that predecessor is indeterminate. Does not check: security or resilience themselves, which MEASURE 2.7 asks to be evaluated and documented; the rule identifies what such an evaluation is about.","reference":"NIST AI RMF 1.0 MEASURE 2.7","require_environment_pinned":true,"require_learned_state_components":true,"require_state_kept":true,"rule_id":"nist-ai-rmf-security-resilience","severity":"mandatory","type":"execution_integrity"},{"description":"The record is traceable and tamper-evident. Checks: the lineage is at least one record long, the training input is committed by a Merkle root (so a record that declares its training input not held or not disclosed fails), and a record with predecessors names the one before it by hash. Does not check: that the committed input is the data actually used; whether the lineage was verified back to its origin, which this rule does not ask for, so a successor evaluated without its predecessors is not failed for it; or the rest of what MEASURE 2.8 asks to be documented.","minimum_chain_length":1,"reference":"NIST AI RMF 1.0 MEASURE 2.8","require_tamper_evident":true,"rule_id":"nist-ai-rmf-transparency-accountability","severity":"recommended","type":"audit_integrity"},{"description":"The provenance of a system obtained from a third party is attested at software level or stronger, so a deployer mapping third-party technology has more than a self-assertion to go on. Checks: the record declares an attestation_level of software or stronger. Does not check: that the issuer attests at that level in fact, where the technology came from, or the rest of what MAP 4.1 asks. The level is the issuer's own claim about itself, and what the trust store grants the signing key is the verifier's trust.attestation check, before any pack is evaluated.","minimum_level":"software","reference":"NIST AI RMF 1.0 MAP 4.1","rule_id":"nist-ai-rmf-third-party-provenance","severity":"recommended","type":"attestation_level"}],"version":"0.1"}

pack.text: {"authority":{"authority_id":"khalm-reference-packs","authority_name":"KHALM reference packs"},"description":"ISO/IEC 42001:2023 (AI management systems), in the part a v0.1 Verifiable Model Record can answer: the Annex A controls on event logs and data provenance, technical documentation and suppliers. The control numbers and titles were checked against public summaries of Annex A that agree with each other, not against the standard's own text, which this pack's author could not read; they must be checked against it.","disclaimer":"A reference implementation of the VMR policy-pack format, not legal advice, not an official instrument and not a certification. Checks: the lineage is at least one record long; the training input is committed by a Merkle root over at least one input, and the root is not that of an empty tree, so a record that declares its training input not held or not disclosed fails; a record with predecessors names the one before it by hash; training does not end before it starts or after the record was issued, and the collection period does not end before it starts; and the lineage was verified back to the initial record, so a successor evaluated without its predecessors is indeterminate. Does not check: the rest of the documentation A.6.2.7 calls for.","reference":"ISO/IEC 42001:2023 Annex A control A.6.2.7 (AI system technical documentation)","require_environment_pinned":true,"require_learned_state_components":true,"require_state_kept":true,"rule_id":"iso-42001-technical-documentation","severity":"mandatory","type":"execution_integrity"},{"description":"A system obtained from a supplier arrives with an attestation at software level or stronger, so the organisation's supplier controls rest on more than a self-assertion. pack.text: {"authority":{"authority_id":"khalm-reference-packs","authority_name":"KHALM reference packs"},"description":"Runtime attestation evidence, as a KHALM reference profile of IETF RFC 9334, the RATS architecture. Each rule cites a section of RFC 9334 by its number and title. The pack is named for the document it encodes: the TRACE project publishes no clause text this pack could cite, so nothing here is presented as a TRACE requirement, and the TRACE profile will be its own pack when there is text to cite.","disclaimer":"A reference implementation of the VMR policy-pack format, not legal advice and not an official instrument. This pack is NOT published, authored or endorsed by the IETF, the RATS working group, the TRACE project or the Linux Foundation; the references are this pack author's reading of RFC 9334.","jurisdiction":"ietf-rats","pack_id":"khalm-reading-rats-rfc9334-v0.1","pack_version":"1.0.0","rules":[{"description":"The Evidence names the environment it is about. Checks: the training software and the software hash of the environment the learning ran in are declared and not empty, and the software hash parses as a hash; an empty claim is not Evidence, and fails. Does not check: that the claims are true of the environment, which only an appraisal against Reference Values can show.","reference":"IETF RFC 9334 (RATS architecture), section 8.1 (Evidence)","require_environment_pinned":true,"rule_id":"rats-attested-environment","severity":"mandatory","type":"execution_integrity"},{"description":"The Target Environment is measured, not merely named, and agrees with the chain it claims. Checks: the learned state and each of its components carry a parseable hash and a positive size; and a deployment or policy-change record keeps the model of its verified immediate predecessor, the same model_hash, so one evaluated without that predecessor is indeterminate. Does not check: that a root of trust took the measurement, which rats-hardware-rooted-measurement asks for.","reference":"IETF RFC 9334 (RATS architecture), section 3.1 (Two Types of Environments of an Attester)","require_learned_state_components":true,"require_state_kept":true,"rule_id":"rats-target-environment-measured","severity":"mandatory","type":"execution_integrity"},{"description":"A hardware root of trust measured the environment. Checks: a TEE measurement is declared and parses as a hash. RFC 9334 calls the components a Verifier has to trust through Endorsements its roots of trust (section 7.4). A record emitted without a TEE signs an empty tee_measurement, which declares that no TEE measured it, so this rule fails on it; the rule is recommended, so that failure does not move the pack's overall status. pack.text: {"authority":{"authority_id":"khalm-reference-packs","authority_name":"KHALM reference packs"},"description":"Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 (the AI Act) as published in the Official Journal, in the part a v0.1 Verifiable Model Record can answer. As published, Art. 113 applies the high-risk obligations from 2 August 2026, and those tied to Art. 6(1) from 2 August 2027. Regulation (EU) 2026/1744 (the Digital Omnibus on AI, in force from 27 July 2026) amends those dates: this pack's author found it on EUR-Lex, giving 2 December 2027 for Annex III systems and 2 August 2028 for Annex I systems. On 14 September 2026 the citations here were checked against the Official Journal texts of Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 and of its amendment Regulation (EU) 2026/1744, and they refer to Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 as amended; the check was a reading comparison, not legal advice. Art. 10 (data and data governance) and Art. 14 (human oversight) are encoded only as recommended rules that check that a record pins its issuer's documentation for each by hash: a pinned document shows which document the issuer relied on, not that the article is met, and no rule here reads what a document says.","disclaimer":"A reference implementation of the VMR policy-pack format, not legal advice and not an official instrument. The clause references are this pack author's reading of the cited text; the European Union, the European AI Office and the national market surveillance authorities have neither authored nor endorsed this pack. Compliance with the AI Act is broader than any document can check.","jurisdiction":"eu","pack_id":"khalm-reading-eu-ai-act-2026","pack_version":"1.0.0","rules":[{"description":"The record belongs to a lineage of records that is kept, ordered and traced to its origin. Checks: the lineage is at least one record long; the training input is committed by a Merkle root, and a record that declares its training input not held or not disclosed fails; a record with predecessors names the one before it by hash; training does not end before it starts or after the record was issued, and the collection period does not end before it starts; and the lineage was verified back to the initial record, so a successor evaluated without its predecessors is indeterminate. Does not check: the events of the system in operation. Art. 12 asks for the automatic recording of events over the system's lifetime; reading a lineage of records, which notes each change to the model (12(2)(a): substantial modifications), as part of that record-keeping is this pack's reading, and it is narrower than the logs Art. 12 requires.","minimum_chain_length":1,"reference":"Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 (AI Act) Art. 12(1) and 12(2)(a)","require_ordered_record":true,"require_tamper_evident":true,"require_verified_lineage":true,"rule_id":"eu-ai-act-record-keeping","severity":"mandatory","type":"audit_integrity"},{"description":"What was learned is pinned, so the system deployed can be shown to be the system whose accuracy and robustness were assessed. Checks: the learned state and each of its components carry a parseable hash and a positive size; and a deployment or policy-change record keeps the model of its verified immediate predecessor, the same model_hash, so one evaluated without that predecessor is indeterminate. Does not check: accuracy or robustness themselves, which Art. 15(1) requires at an appropriate level. The rule identifies the system; it does not measure it.","reference":"Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 (AI Act) Art. 15(1)","require_learned_state_components":true,"require_state_kept":true,"rule_id":"eu-ai-act-accuracy-robustness","severity":"mandatory","type":"execution_integrity"},{"description":"The development environment is identified in the technical documentation. Checks: the training software and the software hash of the environment the learning ran in are declared and not empty, and the software hash parses as a hash; an empty value, which is how a record says there is none, fails. Does not check: that the hash is the hash of the software actually used, or the rest of what Annex IV point 1(c) asks for. Annex IV point 1(c) asks for the versions of relevant software; pinning the software stack by hash as well is this pack's reading.","reference":"Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 (AI Act) Art. 11(1) and Annex IV(1)(c)","require_environment_pinned":true,"rule_id":"eu-ai-act-technical-documentation","severity":"mandatory","type":"execution_integrity"},{"description":"The issuer attests at software level or stronger, so the record resists alteration by a party that is not the provider. Art. 15(5) requires resilience against unauthorised third parties who try to alter a system's use, outputs or performance; choosing attestation as the means is this pack's reading, which is why the rule is recommended rather than mandatory. Checks: the record declares an attestation_level of software or stronger. Does not check: the resilience Art. 15(5) asks for, or the technical solutions it asks to be built in. The level is the issuer's own claim about itself, and what the trust store grants the signing key is the verifier's trust.attestation check, before any pack is evaluated.","minimum_level":"software","reference":"Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 (AI Act) Art. 15(5)","rule_id":"eu-ai-act-cybersecurity-attestation","severity":"recommended","type":"attestation_level"},{"description":"The record pins, by SHA-256, the document its issuer names as its data governance documentation. Checks: the record carries data_governance, and its documentation_hash is a hash; a record without the member declares that it pins no such document, and fails. Does not check: that the document exists, can be obtained or says anything, or that the data governance and management practices of Art. 10(2), or the qualities Art. 10(3) and 10(4) ask of the data sets, are in place or adequate. A pinned document shows which document the issuer relied on, not that it complies. Annex IV(2)(d) puts datasheets of the training data into the technical documentation; reading the pinned document as that part of it is this pack's reading, which is why the rule is recommended rather than mandatory.","document":"data_governance","reference":"Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 (AI Act) Art. 10(2) and Annex IV(2)(d)","rule_id":"eu-ai-act-data-governance","severity":"recommended","type":"documentation_declared"},{"description":"The record pins, by SHA-256, the document its issuer names as its human oversight documentation. Checks: the record carries human_oversight, and its documentation_hash is a hash; a record without the member declares that it pins no such document, and fails. Does not check: that the document exists, can be obtained or says anything, that the oversight measures of Art. 14(3) are built in or identified, or that natural persons can oversee the system as Art. 14(4) requires. A pinned document shows which document the issuer relied on, not that it complies. Annex IV(2)(e) puts the assessment of those measures into the technical documentation; reading the pinned document as that assessment is this pack's reading, which is why the rule is recommended rather than mandatory.","document":"human_oversight","reference":"Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 (AI Act) Art. 14(3) and Annex IV(2)(e)","rule_id":"eu-ai-act-human-oversight","severity":"recommended","type":"documentation_declared"}],"version":"0.1"}

pack.text: {"authority":{"authority_id":"khalm-reference-packs","authority_name":"KHALM reference packs"},"description":"The C2PA content-credentials model applied to the model itself: a claim is signed by a credential a relying party can check, the thing claimed about is bound by hash, and the model that produced generated content is identified. Sections are cited by name rather than by number, because C2PA renumbers between revisions. The section titles were read from the table of contents of the 2.2 specification as published at spec.c2pa.org, not from its full text, and the digitalSourceType value trainedAlgorithmicMedia was confirmed in the C2PA 2.2 Implementation Guidance rather than in the specification itself: both must be checked against the specification.","disclaimer":"A reference implementation of the VMR policy-pack format, not legal advice and not an official instrument. The references are this pack author's reading of the cited specification; the Coalition for Content Provenance and Authenticity has neither authored nor endorsed this pack, and this pack is not a C2PA conformance test.","jurisdiction":"c2pa","pack_id":"khalm-reading-c2pa-ai-disclosure-2.2","pack_version":"1.0.0","rules":[{"description":"The claim is signed by a credential a relying party can evaluate, not merely by whoever held a key. Checks: the record declares an attestation_level of software or stronger. Does not check: that the issuer attests at that level in fact. The level is the issuer's own claim about itself, and this rule reads only that claim; what the trust store grants the signing key is a different question, which the verifier answers (trust.attestation) before any pack is evaluated. No C2PA credential, certificate chain or conformance program is examined here.","minimum_level":"software","reference":"C2PA Technical Specification 2.2, Signing a Claim, and Digital Signatures","rule_id":"c2pa-claim-signature","severity":"mandatory","type":"attestation_level"},{"description":"What the claim is about is bound to it by hash, the way a C2PA hard binding binds an asset. Checks: the training input is committed by a Merkle root over at least one input, and the root is not that of an empty tree, so a record that declares its training input not held or not disclosed fails; and a record with predecessors names the one before it by hash. Does not check: that the committed input is the content the claim describes; a record carries no c2pa.hash.data assertion of its own.","reference":"C2PA Technical Specification 2.2, Hard Bindings (the c2pa.hash.data assertion)","require_input_committed":true,"require_tamper_evident":true,"rule_id":"c2pa-hard-binding","severity":"mandatory","type":"audit_integrity"},{"description":"The model named as the generator of trained-algorithmic media is identified by more than a name. Checks: its learned state and each component carry a parseable hash and a positive size. Does not check: that any bytes hash to a declared value, since an evaluation reads the record and nothing else; or that this model produced any particular content. A record carries no c2pa.actions assertion of its own: the rule identifies the model, it does not tie it to an asset.","reference":"C2PA Technical Specification 2.2, the c2pa.actions assertion with digitalSourceType trainedAlgorithmicMedia","require_learned_state_components":true,"rule_id":"c2pa-generator-identified","severity":"recommended","type":"execution_integrity"}],"version":"0.1"}

pack.text: {"authority":{"authority_id":"khalm-reference-packs","authority_name":"KHALM reference packs"},"description":"Runtime attestation evidence, as a KHALM reference profile of IETF RFC 9334, the RATS architecture. Each rule cites a section of RFC 9334 by its number and title. The pack is named for the document it encodes: the TRACE project publishes no clause text this pack could cite, so nothing here is presented as a TRACE requirement, and the TRACE profile will be its own pack when there is text to cite.","disclaimer":"A reference implementation of the VMR policy-pack format, not legal advice and not an official instrument. This pack is NOT published, authored or endorsed by the IETF, the RATS working group, the TRACE project or the Linux Foundation; the references are this pack author's reading of RFC 9334.","jurisdiction":"ietf-rats","pack_id":"khalm-reading-rats-rfc9334-v0.1","pack_version":"1.0.0","rules":[{"description":"The Evidence names the environment it is about. Checks: the training software and the software hash of the environment the learning ran in are declared and not empty, and the software hash parses as a hash; an empty claim is not Evidence, and fails. Does not check: that the claims are true of the environment, which only an appraisal against Reference Values can show.","reference":"IETF RFC 9334 (RATS architecture), section 8.1 (Evidence)","require_environment_pinned":true,"rule_id":"rats-attested-environment","severity":"mandatory","type":"execution_integrity"},{"description":"The Target Environment is measured, not merely named, and agrees with the chain it claims. Checks: the learned state and each of its components carry a parseable hash and a positive size; and a deployment or policy-change record keeps the model of its verified immediate predecessor, the same model_hash, so one evaluated without that predecessor is indeterminate. Does not check: that a root of trust took the measurement, which rats-hardware-rooted-measurement asks for.","reference":"IETF RFC 9334 (RATS architecture), section 3.1 (Two Types of Environments of an Attester)","require_learned_state_components":true,"require_state_kept":true,"rule_id":"rats-target-environment-measured","severity":"mandatory","type":"execution_integrity"},{"description":"A hardware root of trust measured the environment. Checks: a TEE measurement is declared and parses as a hash. RFC 9334 calls the components a Verifier has to trust through Endorsements its roots of trust (section 7.4). A record emitted without a TEE signs an empty tee_measurement, which declares that no TEE measured it, so this rule fails on it; the rule is recommended, so that failure does not move the pack's overall status. Does not check: that a root of trust took the measurement, or that the value is the measurement of any environment. Only an appraisal against Reference Values can show that, and a v0.1 record carries neither Endorsements nor Reference Values.","reference":"IETF RFC 9334 (RATS architecture), section 7.4 (Verifier: roots of trust)","require_tee":true,"rule_id":"rats-hardware-rooted-measurement","severity":"recommended","type":"execution_integrity"},{"description":"The Evidence is integrity-protected and linked rather than standing alone. Checks: the lineage is at least one record long, the training input is committed by a Merkle root (so a record that declares its training input not held or not disclosed fails), and a record with predecessors names the one before it by hash. Section 12.2 asks that conveyed Evidence be integrity-protected; this hash chain is this pack's reading of that for a record. Does not check: freshness in RFC 9334's sense (section 10: that Evidence is recent), because a v0.1 record carries no nonce or epoch; that the committed input is the data the Evidence is about; or whether the lineage was verified back to its origin, which this rule does not ask for.","minimum_chain_length":1,"reference":"IETF RFC 9334 (RATS architecture), section 12.2 (Conceptual Message Protection)","require_tamper_evident":true,"rule_id":"rats-evidence-integrity","severity":"recommended","type":"audit_integrity"},{"description":"The Attester is identified by a key a Verifier can evaluate. Checks: the record declares an attestation_level of software or stronger. Does not check: that an Attester in RFC 9334's sense produced the Evidence, or that the declared level is true of it. The level is the issuer's own claim about itself, and what the trust store grants the signing key is the verifier's trust.attestation check, before any pack is evaluated; a v0.1 record carries no Endorsement a Verifier could appraise the key against.","minimum_level":"software","reference":"IETF RFC 9334 (RATS architecture), sections 7 (Trust Model) and 7.4 (Verifier)","rule_id":"rats-attester-identity","severity":"recommended","type":"attestation_level"}],"version":"0.1"}
